turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Why did my cake sink in the middle?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The most common reason is opening the oven door too early. The cake hasn't set yet, and the cool air makes it collapse.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I did peek / at about fifteen minutes.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That might be it. Wait until at least three quarters of the baking time before you open the door.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Could it be anything else?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Too much baking powder or underbaking can also do it. Check the center with a toothpick, it should come out clean.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay. I'll try again next weekend.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good luck. A sunken cake still tastes great, so enjoy this one anyway.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I swap regular flour for whole wheat in my muffin recipe?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You can, but start by swapping only half. Whole wheat makes muffins denser and a little drier.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I add more liquid then?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, a couple of extra spoonfuls of milk helps. Letting the batter rest ten minutes also softens the bran.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And if I want to cut / some of the sugar too?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You can cut about a quarter without problems. Mashed banana or a bit of applesauce adds sweetness back.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Banana sounds good. I have some brown ones.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Perfect, the browner the better for baking.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don't have buttermilk and the recipe needs it. Any way around that?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Easy fix. Stir a tablespoon of lemon juice or vinegar into a cup of regular milk and let it sit five minutes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It'll curdle, right? Is that okay?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's exactly what you want. It thickens and gets tangy like buttermilk.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Great. Oh, and I'm also / out of eggs. Is that a disaster?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not for most cakes. A quarter cup of plain yogurt or mashed banana can replace one egg.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I have yogurt. Okay, I'm saved.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Nice save. Enjoy your baking.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm a student with a tiny oven. Can I still bake cookies?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Definitely. Bake them in smaller batches on one tray in the middle of the oven, so they cook evenly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don't have / a mixer or anything fancy.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You don't need one. Melted butter cookies can be mixed with just a spoon and a bowl.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh nice. How long do they take?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Usually ten to twelve minutes. Take them out when the edges are golden and the middle still looks soft.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They won't be raw?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: They keep cooking on the hot tray for a few minutes. That's the secret to chewy cookies.
